findings.title: Recovery codes are passed unhashed to user-storage credential update, enabling plaintext storage
findings.body: createRecoveryCodesCredential() builds a UserCredentialModel from the raw/unhashed `generatedCodes` list (JSON-serialized) and hands it to user.credentialManager().updateCredential(), while the local-DB fallback path uses `credentialModel`, which already contains hashed codes. Nothing in the API/contract requires a UserStorageProvider implementing updateCredential() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE to hash the raw value before persisting it (unlike the Password case, which explicitly hashes via PasswordHashProvider). The reference implementation shipped in this very PR (BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential/isValid) indeed stores and compares the raw codes verbatim with no hashing at all, meaning recovery codes end up persisted in plaintext when backed by user storage, unlike the hashed codes stored for local-DB users. This is a security regression/inconsistency for a feature whose whole purpose is one-time secret codes.

findings.title: getCredentials() loses the stored credential id and userLabel for recovery codes
findings.body: In getCredentials(), the OTP branch returns the actually stored CredentialModel object (myUser.getOtp()), preserving its id. The recovery-codes branch instead builds a brand new RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel via createFromValues(...) and never copies over myUser.recoveryCodes.getId() (which was set in updateCredential() via KeycloakModelUtils.generateId()). As a result, the credential model returned to callers (e.g. RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential -> RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator) has a different/undefined id than the one actually stored. Any subsequent operation that references the credential by this id (e.g. authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId()) in RecoveryAuthnCodesFormAuthenticator.action() when allCodesUsed()) will fail to locate/remove the real stored credential, since the id doesn't match. Additionally, myUser.recoveryCodes.getUserLabel() is read here but userLabel is never set in updateCredential(), so it is always null.

findings.title: Recovery codes stored via user storage are never consumed, breaking single-use guarantee
findings.body: isValid() for RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE only checks whether the submitted code exists in the stored list (generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(...)); it never removes or flags the matched code as used, nor persists any updated state back into myUser.recoveryCodes. Consequently, a recovery code backed by this user storage provider can be reused an unlimited number of times, unlike the local/DB-backed implementation where recovery codes are intended to be single-use (RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.allCodesUsed() logic depends on per-code consumption). This defeats a core security property of recovery/backup codes for any user whose credentials are stored via a UserStorageProvider following this pattern.

findings.title: getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() not updated for recovery codes
findings.body: This PR adds RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE support to supportsCredentialType, updateCredential, isConfiguredFor, isValid and getCredentials, but getDisableableCredentialTypesStream() (lines 255-264) still only ever returns CredentialModel.OTP. As a result, a user whose recovery codes are stored in this user-storage provider can never have that credential listed/disabled through the standard disable-credential API/UI, unlike OTP, leaving the new feature only partially wired up.

findings.title: New test does not verify single-use/exhaustion behaviour of recovery codes in user storage
findings.body: testRecoveryKeysSetupAndLogin() only performs a single successful login using one recovery code and then logs out; it never attempts to reuse the same code, nor exhausts all codes to verify that the CONFIGURE_RECOVERY_AUTHN_CODES required action is re-triggered. Given that BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid() never marks codes as consumed (see related finding), this test suite does not catch that regression, so the single-use guarantee for recovery codes stored via user storage is effectively untested.

findings.title: getCredentials() can NPE if user is not present in the backing map
findings.body: getCredentials() calls `var myUser = getMyUser(user);` and immediately dereferences `myUser.recoveryCodes` / `myUser.otp` without a null check, unlike isConfiguredFor() and isValid() in the same class which explicitly guard with `if (myUser == null) return false;`. If this method is ever invoked for a user no longer present in the in-memory map, it will throw a NullPointerException instead of returning an empty stream.
